info.title: Finance App API
info.description:
Personal finance management platform.

This document is **generated from the running Express app** by `npm run generate:openapi`, so the paths, parameters and request bodies below are the ones the server actually enforces. It is committed to the repository and checked in CI, which is what stops it from drifting.

Money crosses this API as a **decimal string**, never a JSON number. Every amount is stored as `NUMERIC(19,4)`.

Response bodies are not described yet — that is phase 2.

bearerAuth.description: A short-lived access token from `POST /api/v1/auth/login` or `/auth/refresh`. Refresh tokens are opaque, rotate on every use, and are tracked in families.

code.description: The stable, machine-readable member of the error taxonomy.

message.description: A sentence for a person, rendered in the locale resolved from the profile or `Accept-Language`. Match on `code`, never on this.

details.description: Present on a field-validation failure: one entry per rejected field.

path.description: Dotted path, prefixed by the request part: `body.name`.

requestId.description: Correlates the response with the server log line; also sent as `x-request-id`.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed — unparseable JSON, or a value the database refused outright.

Unauthorized.description: No bearer token was sent, or it has expired or belongs to an inactive account.

Forbidden.description: The caller is authenticated but lacks the required role in this workspace.

NotFound.description: No such resource, or none the caller is allowed to know exists.

Conflict.description: The write collided with an existing row, such as a duplicate name.

ValidationFailed.description: One or more fields were rejected. `error.details` names each one, already translated into the language resolved for the request.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests; the caller has exceeded the rate limit for this window.

InternalError.description: Something failed inside the API. The message is fixed and the detail stays in the logs.
